22359-an-essay-on-professional-ethics-se.title: An Essay On Professional Ethics.
22359-an-essay-on-professional-ethics-se.creator: George Sharswood.
22359-an-essay-on-professional-ethics-se.description: A book by George Sharswood.. Essay was originally published under the title of "A Compend of Lectures on the Aims and Duties of the Profession of the Law, delivered before the Law Class of the University of Pennsylvania." A portion of it had been read by the author as an Introductory Lecture at the opening of the Fifth Session of the Law Department of that Institution, October 2d, 1854.

arxiv-2011-12249.title: Generalizing Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution Across Multiple Corpora
arxiv-2011-12249.creator: Michael Bugert, Nils Reimers, Iryna Gurevych
arxiv-2011-12249.description: Abstract Cross-document event coreference resolution (CDCR) is an NLP task in which mentions of events need to be identified and clustered throughout a collection of documents. CDCR aims to benefit downstream multi-document applications, but despite recent progress on corpora and system development, downstream improvements from applying CDCR have not been shown yet.

arxiv-2012-15254.title: Quantum Multi-Solution Bernoulli Search with Applications to Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum Security
arxiv-2012-15254.creator: Alexandru Cojocaru, Juan Garay, Aggelos Kiayias, Fang Song, Petros Wallden
arxiv-2012-15254.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Alexandru Cojocaru, Juan Garay, Aggelos Kiayias, Fang Song, Petros Wallden. A proof of work (PoW) is an important cryptographic construct which enables a party to convince other parties that they have invested some effort in solving a computational task.

arxiv-2106-01486.title: On an integral representation of the normalized trace of the k k -th symmetric tensor power of matrices and some applications
arxiv-2106-01486.creator: Hassan Issa ∗, Hassan Abbas ∗, Bassam Mourad ∗
arxiv-2106-01486.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hassan Issa ∗, Hassan Abbas ∗, Bassam Mourad ∗. Let A A be an n × n n\times n matrix and let ∨ k A \vee^{k}A be its k k -th symmetric tensor product. We express the normalized trace of ∨ k A \vee^{k}A as an integral of the k k -th powers of the numerical values of A A over the unit sphere 𝕊 n \mathbb{S}^{n} of ℂ n \mathbb{C}^{n} with respect to the normalized Euclidean surface measure.

arxiv-2107-11842.creator: Mihalis Maliakas, Dimitra-Dionysia Stergiopoulou

arxiv-2211-11707.title: A tactile model of the night summer northern sky for the teaching of astronomy to the BVI
arxiv-2211-11707.creator: Pérez-Montero, E.
arxiv-2211-11707.description: Abstract Abstract Astroaccesible is an outreach project hosted by the Instituto de Astrofísica de Andalucía - CSIC aimed at the teaching and popularisation of the astronomy among all publics independently of their capabilities and abilities, paying special attention to the collective of blind and visually impaired (BVI).

arxiv-2306-03396.title: The non-standard Lagrangian from non-uniqueness principle of the real scalar field and fermion field
arxiv-2306-03396.creator: Suppanat Supanyo 1,2, Monsit Tanasittikosol 1,2, Sikarin Yoo-Kong 3
arxiv-2306-03396.description: Abstract We construct the non-standard Lagrangian, called the multiplicative form, of the homogeneous scalar field and fermion field through the inverse calculus of variations, which the equation of motion still satisfies the Klein-Gordon and Dirac equations, respectively. By employing the non-uniqueness of Lagrangian, we show that the Lagrangians can be written between the linear combination of standard and non-standard Lagrangian.

arxiv-2306-08278.title: Uplink Performance of RIS-aided Cell-Free Massive MIMO System with Electromagnetic Interference Thanks: E. Shi and J. Zhang are with the School of Electronics and Information Engineering, Beijing Jiaotong University, Beijing 100044, P. R. China. (e-mail: jiayizhang@bjtu.edu.cn). Thanks: D. W. K. Ng
arxiv-2306-08278.creator: Enyu Shi, Jiayi Zhang
arxiv-2306-08278.description: Abstract Cell-free (CF) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) and reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) are two promising technologies for realizing future beyond-fifth generation (B5G) networks. In this paper, we consider a practical spatially correlated RIS-aided CF massive MIMO system with multi-antenna access points (APs) over spatially correlated fading channels.

arxiv-2403-07413.title: Learning-Augmented Algorithms with Explicit Predictors
arxiv-2403-07413.creator: Marek Eliáš, Haim Kaplan, Yishay Mansour, Shay Moran
arxiv-2403-07413.description: Abstract Recent advances in algorithmic design show how to utilize predictions obtained by machine learning models from past and present data. These approaches have demonstrated an enhancement in performance when the predictions are accurate, while also ensuring robustness by providing worst-case guarantees when predictions fail.

arxiv-2406-04758.title: Think out Loud: Emotion Deducing Explanation in Dialogues
arxiv-2406-04758.creator: Jiangnan Li, Zheng Lin, Lanrui Wang, Qingyi Si, Yanan Cao, Mo Yu, Peng Fu, Weiping Wang, Jie Zhou
arxiv-2406-04758.description: Abstract Humans convey emotions through daily dialogues, making emotion understanding a crucial step of affective intelligence. To understand emotions in dialogues, machines are asked to recognize the emotion for an utterance (Emotion Recognition in Dialogues, ERD); based on the emotion, then find causal utterances for the emotion (Emotion Cause Extraction in Dialogues, ECED).

arxiv-2407-04355.title: Data-Driven Tissue- and Subject-Specific Elastic Regularization for Medical Image Registration
arxiv-2407-04355.creator: Anna Reithmeir, Lina Felsner, Rickmer Braren, Julia A. Schnabel, Veronika A. Zimmer
arxiv-2407-04355.description: Abstract Physics-inspired regularization is desired for intra-patient image registration since it can effectively capture the biomechanical characteristics of anatomical structures. However, a major challenge lies in the reliance on physical parameters: Parameter estimations vary widely across the literature, and the physical properties themselves are inherently subject-specific.

arxiv-2409-15193.title: Fractonic coset construction for spontaneously broken translations
arxiv-2409-15193.creator: Ameya Chavda, Daniel Naegels, John Staunton
arxiv-2409-15193.description: Abstract We study the homogeneous breaking of spatial translation symmetry concomitantly with the spontaneous breaking of other internal and spacetime symmetries, including dilations. We use the symmetry-breaking pattern as the only input to derive, via the coset construction, general effective field theories for the symmetry-originated modes associated with Goldstone’s theorem, namely the Nambu-Goldstone candidates.

arxiv-2503-02381.title: Secondary terms in the counting functions of quartic fields I
arxiv-2503-02381.creator: Arul Shankar, Jacob Tsimerman
arxiv-2503-02381.description: Abstract We prove that the smoothed counting function of the set of quartic fields, satisfying any finite set of local conditions, can be written as a linear combination of X , X 5 / 6 ​ log ⁡ X , X 5 / 6 X,X^{5/6}\log X,X^{5/6} , upto an error term of O ⁡ ( X 13 / 16 +

arxiv-2505-10649.title: Advancing Multiple Instance Learning with Continual Learning for Whole Slide Imaging
arxiv-2505-10649.creator: Xianrui Li, Yufei Cui, Jun Li, Antoni B. Chan
arxiv-2505-10649.description: Abstract Advances in medical imaging and deep learning have propelled progress in whole slide image (WSI) analysis, with multiple instance learning (MIL) showing promise for efficient and accurate diagnostics. However, conventional MIL models often lack adaptability to evolving datasets, as they rely on static training that cannot incorporate new information without extensive retraining.

arxiv-2508-15706.title: Communication Efficient LLM Pre-training with SparseLoCo
arxiv-2508-15706.creator: Amir Sarfi, Benjamin Thérien, Joel Lidin, Eugene Belilovsky
arxiv-2508-15706.description: Abstract Communication-efficient distributed training algorithms have received considerable interest recently due to their benefits for training Large Language Models (LLMs) in bandwidth-constrained settings, such as across data centers and over the internet. Despite reducing communication frequency, these methods still typically require communicating a full copy of the model’s gradients—resulting in a communication bottleneck even for cross-datacenter links.

arxiv-2602-11336.title: Traffic Flow Reconstruction from Limited Collected Data
arxiv-2602-11336.creator: Nail Baloul, Amaury Hayat, Thibault Liard and Pierre Lissy
arxiv-2602-11336.description: Abstract We propose an efficient method for reconstructing traffic density with low penetration rate of probe vehicles. Specifically, we rely on measuring only the initial and final positions of a small number of cars which are generated using microscopic dynamical systems. We then implement a machine learning algorithm from scratch to reconstruct the approximate traffic density.

pmc-10737809.title: EMBOLDEN: CATALYZING RESEARCH FOR OLDER ADULTS THROUGH CO-DESIGNED MOBILITY-PROMOTING INTERVENTION RESEARCH
pmc-10737809.creator: Rebecca Ganann, Caroline Moore, Stuart Phillips, Elizabeth Alvarez, Bruce Newbold, Sarah Neil-Sztramko, Maggie MacNeil, Kathryn Fisher
pmc-10737809.description: Mobility and social participation are requisites for optimizing health, independence, and quality of life in older populations. Most mobility-enhancing interventions for older adults have been designed by researchers alone, which often experience implementation challenges and limited effectiveness when translated to real-world contexts.

pmc-11430398.title: The Oncoprotein Fra-2 Drives the Activation of Human Endogenous Retrovirus Env Expression in Adult T-Cell Leukemia/Lymphoma (ATLL) Patients
pmc-11430398.creator: Julie Tram, Laetitia Marty, Célima Mourouvin, Magali Abrantes, Ilham Jaafari, Raymond Césaire, Philippe Hélias, Benoit Barbeau, Jean-Michel Mesnard, Véronique Baccini, Laurent Chaloin, Jean-Marie Jr. Peloponese
pmc-11430398.description: Human endogenous retroviruses (HERVs) are retroviral sequences integrated into 8% of the human genome resulting from ancient exogenous retroviral infections. Unlike endogenous retroviruses of other mammalian species, HERVs are mostly replication and retro-transposition defective, and their transcription is strictly regulated by epigenetic mechanisms in normal cells.

pmc-11585616.title: Allosteric substrate release by a sialic acid TRAP transporter substrate binding protein
pmc-11585616.creator: Niels Schneberger, Philipp Hendricks, Martin F. Peter, Erik Gehrke, Sophie C. Binder, Paul-Albert Koenig, Stephan Menzel, Gavin H. Thomas, Gregor Hagelueken
pmc-11585616.description: The tripartite ATP-independent periplasmic (TRAP) transporters enable Vibrio cholerae and Haemophilus influenzae to acquire sialic acid, aiding their colonization of human hosts. This process depends on SiaP, a substrate-binding protein (SBP) that captures and delivers sialic acid to the transporter. We identified 11 nanobodies that bind specifically to the SiaP proteins from H. influenzae (HiSiaP) and V. cholerae (VcSiaP).

pmc-12466369.title: Critical Review of Glyphosate-Induced Oxidative and Hormonal Testicular Disruption
pmc-12466369.creator: Sara R Branco, Marco G Alves, Pedro Fontes Oliveira, Ariane Zamoner, Alessandra Napolitano
pmc-12466369.description: Glyphosate, the active ingredient in many herbicides, has been extensively used in agricultural practices worldwide, leading to environmental persistence of the herbicide and its main metabolite, aminomethylphosphonic acid (AMPA), particularly in water and soil. Despite a short half-life in biological fluids, frequent detection of glyphosate and AMPA in urine samples suggests ongoing human exposure.

pmc-13224867.title: Defective HNF1A hinders GLI3 processing favoring duodenal versus pancreatic fate, thus leading to intestinal elongation in vivo
pmc-13224867.creator: Lucas Unger, Ulrik Larsen, Thomas Aga Legøy, Md Kaykobad Hossain, June Helen Gudmestad, Amanda Friestad, Shayla Sharmine, Pål Rasmus Njølstad, Helge Ræder, Pedro Luis Herrera, Luiza Ghila, Simona Chera
pmc-13224867.description: In this study, Unger et al. identify an autoregulatory loop between HNF1A and Hedgehog signaling that biases stem cells toward either duodenal or pancreatic lineage identities. Mutant HNF1A—through disruption of GLI3 processing by cilium proteins—controls selective gene expression, as well as that of itself, responsible for lineage segregation in the liver, pancreas, and gut.

pmc-13407376.title: Fentanyl Induces Behavioral Sensitization and Decreases Class IIa HDAC Expression-Activity in Brain as Measured by [18F]TFAHA PET Imaging in Female and Male Rats
pmc-13407376.creator: Cameron J. Davidson, Itzick Nahmoud, Mahmoud Teran, Erek Binkowski, Nareen Sadik, Majd A. Yahya, Susanne Brummelte, Alana C. Conti, Nerissa T. Viola, Srinivasu Kallakuri, Shane A. Perrine
pmc-13407376.description: Background: Although fentanyl significantly contributes to opioid-related morbidity and mortality, little is known about the epigenetic changes that may influence long-term neuronal adaptations. Objective: The effects of repeated fentanyl administration on class IIa histone deacetylase (HDAC) expression-activity were studied using the radiotracer [18F]TFAHA and positron emission tomography (PET) imaging in a model of fentanyl-induced behavioral sensitization.

pmc-13415663.title: Letter to the Editor: C2 schwannoma resection
pmc-13415663.creator: Atul Goel

pmc-13538953.title: Frailty Scores and Ethical Decision‐Making in Critical Care: Lessons From the COVID‐19 Pandemic
pmc-13538953.creator: Chukwuka Elendu, Chidera A Okezie‐Okoye, Ahmed I Ali, Emeka H Okolo, Mirabel A Bell‐Gam, Kiranraj Ravikumar, Favour K Mbakwe
pmc-13538953.description: Frailty scores should support, not replace, individualized critical care decisions, as the COVID‐19 pandemic exposed the ethical limitations of rigid frailty‐based triage, particularly among older adults and individuals with chronic disability. Meaningful recovery may occur despite severe illness, reinforcing the importance of patient autonomy, multidisciplinary assessment, and holistic clinical judgment.

pmc-13556737.title: 403. Sustained administration of the full and partial agonists of trace amine associated receptor 1 (TAAR1) induces different effects on the excitability of central monoaminergic neurons
pmc-13556737.creator: T Khoury, D Grinchii, M C Hoener, E Dremencov
pmc-13556737.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundTrace amine associated receptor 1 (TAAR1) is a promising target for the next generation of the central nervous system (CNS) drugs. It has been previously shown that the full (RO5256390) and partial (RO5263397) agonists of TAAR1 had anti-addictive, pro-cognitive, and antipsychotic- and antidepressant-like effects; these beneficial effects of TAAR1 ligands were linked, at least in part, with the altered excitability of serotonergic (5-HT) neurons of the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) and dopaminergic neurons of the ventral terminal area (VTA; Revel et al

pmc-13582400.title: Radiomics and deep learning for intracranial aneurysm rupture-status assessment on CTA/MRA: a multicenter retrospective study
pmc-13582400.creator: Tao Wang, Jiang Fan, Yi He, Changren Huang, Kunyang Bao
pmc-13582400.description: BackgroundRupture of intracranial aneurysms leads to aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage with severe adverse outcomes. Current retrospective imaging studies merely differentiate existing ruptured and unruptured aneurysms instead of forecasting prospective rupture risk. To address this limitation, we constructed a multimodal fusion model combining handcrafted radiomics and deep learning embeddings from routine CTA/MRA for aneurysm rupture discrimination and performed internal validation.

pmc-13583696.title: Labour induction in low-risk women at 39 weeks of gestation: a randomised trial in China (LIRIC) – protocol of an open label, randomised controlled trial
pmc-13583696.creator: Huajing Gao, Junhua Shen, Danqing Chen, Ben Willem Mol, Wensheng Hu, Zhaoxia Liang, Xiaoxia Bai, Xiujun Han, Jiajun Zhu, Hong Wang, Xiaozhen Liu, Chang Su, Yuan Chen, Ruopeng Weng, Yifeng Liu, Wentao Li, Dan Zhang
pmc-13583696.description: IntroductionThe A Randomized Trial of Induction Versus Expectant Management (ARRIVE) first demonstrated that elective induction of labour (IOL) at 39 weeks in low-risk pregnancies reduced the likelihood of caesarean section (CS) without compromising perinatal safety; however, the generalisability of these findings remains debated, leading to uncertainty in clinical practice.

pmc-13633621.title: Interdisciplinary modelling approaches for One Health in agri-food systems: a scoping review and conceptual analysis
pmc-13633621.creator: Thomas Art Burke, Antje Risius
pmc-13633621.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundIncreasingly, the One Health approach must be applied to a changing food system to simultaneously support nutritional, infectious disease, and environmental outcomes. Successful interventions by public health authorities will require quantitative modelling for evaluating trade-offs and prioritization.

pmc-13658378.title: Mesh quality comparison of common three file formats derived from intraoral scans
pmc-13658378.creator: Mahmoud E. Elbashti, Gülce Çakmak, Marta Macarena Paz-Cortes, Nadin Al-Haj Husain, Samir Abou-Ayash, Andrea Roccuzzo, Pedro Molinero-Mourelle
pmc-13658378.description: PurposeTo comparatively evaluate mesh quality metrics in PLY, STL, and OBJ files derived from native intraoral scans and exported using different mesh processing software, with emphasis on computational performance, geometric fidelity, and mesh resolution.MethodsFifty maxillary and mandibular full-arch intraoral scan datasets were acquired using a Trios 4 intraoral scanner under clinical conditions.
